resources.string: Screen control
This app can see and control anything on %1$s\'s screen, including typing by itself, pressing buttons by itself, and reading what other apps show, including mobile banking.
Admin rights
This app asks for device administrator rights. That makes it very hard to remove, and lets it lock or wipe everything on %1$s\'s phone.
SMS access
This app can read every SMS that arrives on %1$s\'s phone, including bank OTP codes. With those codes, someone else can get into %1$s\'s account without knowing the password.
Installs apps
This app can install other apps on %1$s\'s phone without being asked. What it installs later can be far more dangerous.
Fake screens
This app can draw fake screens over other apps, for example a copied bank login page to steal %1$s\'s password.
Reads notifications
This app can read every notification that arrives, including SMS contents and OTP codes shown on the lock screen.
Records audio
This app can switch on the microphone and record what is said around %1$s, even while it is not open.
Controls calls
This app can place calls by itself without %1$s knowing, including to premium numbers.
Reads contacts
This app can read %1$s\'s entire contact list. That data is often used to scam family and friends by pretending to be %1$s.
Uses the camera
This app can take photos and video with the camera, even while the screen is not in use.
Tracks location
This app can know exactly where %1$s is, continuously.
Device data
This app can read %1$s\'s phone number and the phone\'s identity.
Lists apps
This app can see every other app installed, including which bank apps %1$s uses.
Starts by itself
This app starts on its own every time the phone is switched on, without %1$s opening it.
Sends data
This app can send data out over the internet. Once sent, that data cannot be taken back.
Keeps running
This app can keep running in the background even after it is closed.
Not from the Play Store
This app was not installed from the Play Store. Files like this usually arrive over WhatsApp or a link, and Google has never checked them.
Hidden icon
This app hides its icon. %1$s will not realise it is on the phone.
Imitates a real app
This app\'s name imitates an official bank or e-wallet app. The real ones are never shared over WhatsApp.
Unofficial signature
This app is not signed by a registered developer, so nobody can be held responsible for it.
Deliberately outdated
This app is built for an old version of Android, a common trick to avoid the permission prompts that should appear.
OTP theft
This app can read %1$s\'s SMS and send it to the internet. This is the pattern used to steal bank OTP codes.
Screen takeover
This app can draw fake screens and press buttons by itself. This is the signature of an account-stealing app.
OTP theft
This app can read notifications containing OTP codes and send them out, without needing SMS permission at all.
Carries other apps
This app came from outside the Play Store and can install other apps on its own.
Hard to remove
This app hides itself and asks for admin rights at the same time, making it very hard to find and remove.
